name: Decentralized Application (dApp) Development
description: Building full-stack decentralized applications that connect users to smart contracts through web or mobile interfaces. Covers the major dApp categories (DeFi, DAOs, NFTs, Payments, Insurance), node-as-a-service providers that replace running your own node, backend language options (JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Go), frontend framework integration, client libraries for blockchain interaction (ethers.js, web3.js, Moralis), and client node types for teams who do run their own infrastructure.

subskills.name: DeFi Applications
subskills.description: Decentralized Finance: on-chain protocols replacing traditional financial intermediaries. Key DeFi primitives: Automated Market Makers (AMMs — Uniswap v2/v3, Curve, Balancer), lending protocols (Aave, Compound — collateralized borrowing, liquidation mechanics, interest rate models), yield aggregators (Yearn Finance — ERC-4626 vaults), stablecoins (MakerDAO DAI — CDP/Vault model, algorithmic), perpetual DEXes (GMX, dYdX), liquid staking (Lido, Rocket Pool — stETH), flash loans (Aave — atomic, uncollateralized). Understanding TVL, composability (money legos), protocol governance via tokens.

subskills.name: DAOs (Decentralized Autonomous Organizations)
subskills.description: On-chain governance structures where token holders vote on protocol decisions. Covers: governance token distribution, proposal lifecycle (creation → voting period → timelock → execution), quorum and voting thresholds, OpenZeppelin Governor framework (GovernorBravo), Compound governance fork, Snapshot (off-chain signaling with on-chain execution), Gnosis Safe multi-sig for treasury management, Tally and Boardroom for DAO UIs, veto and emergency mechanisms, delegate voting, and quadratic voting.

subskills.name: NFTs (Non-Fungible Tokens)
subskills.description: ERC-721 and ERC-1155 token implementations for unique digital assets. Covers: metadata standards (JSON schema, on-chain vs IPFS vs Arweave storage), lazy minting, Dutch auction minting, allowlist (Merkle tree-based whitelists), royalties (ERC-2981 on-chain royalty standard), NFT marketplaces (OpenSea, Blur, LooksRare APIs and seaport protocol), soulbound tokens (ERC-5192 non-transferable), dynamic NFTs (metadata updated by oracles or time), generative art (EVM-based randomness for traits), and NFT fractionalization.

subskills.name: Payments & Insurance dApps
subskills.description: Payment-focused applications: crypto payment gateways (Coinbase Commerce, BTCPay Server), recurring payments via ERC-20 approve-based subscriptions, streaming payments (Superfluid — per-second token streams, SABLIER), request financing (Request Network), stablecoin payments, and Lightning Network for Bitcoin micropayments. Parametric insurance on-chain: smart contracts that automatically pay out when oracle-verified conditions are met (flight delay insurance, crop insurance, protocol cover — Nexus Mutual, InsurAce).

subskills.name: Node-as-a-Service Providers
subskills.description: Infrastructure providers offering managed blockchain node RPC endpoints so developers don't need to run their own nodes. Alchemy (leading provider: Enhanced APIs for NFT metadata, transaction history, Notify webhooks, Transact for gas-optimized transaction sending, Alchemy SDK), Infura (ConsenSys, IPFS gateway included, broad network support), Moralis (Web3 data API — wallet activity, token balances, NFT metadata, Streams for real-time events — abstraction layer over RPC), QuickNode (high-performance RPC, add-ons marketplace), Ankr (decentralized RPC). Comparing rate limits, costs, supported chains, and enhanced APIs.

subskills.name: Backend Languages for dApps (JS, Python, Go)
subskills.description: Server-side code that interacts with blockchains for indexing, automation, and API serving. JavaScript/TypeScript with ethers.js or viem for event listeners, transaction sending, and API servers (Next.js API routes, Express). Python with web3.py for data analysis, bot development, and scripting (DeFi bots, arbitrage). Go with go-ethereum (geth) for high-performance blockchain interaction, building custom indexers, MEV bots, and validator infrastructure. The Graph (subgraph AssemblyScript) for decentralized event indexing.

subskills.name: Frontend Frameworks for dApps
subskills.description: Web frameworks adapted for blockchain frontends. React is dominant: wagmi (React hooks for Ethereum — useAccount, useBalance, useContractRead, useContractWrite, useWaitForTransaction), RainbowKit (wallet connection UI built on wagmi), Viem (TypeScript-first, tree-shakeable ethers.js alternative underlying wagmi v2). Vue with useWeb3 or viem direct. Angular with Web3.js or ethers. Next.js for SSR/SSG of dApp UIs (server-side rendering compatible with client-only wallet connection). React Query for async blockchain state management.

subskills.name: Client Libraries — ethers.js, web3.js, Moralis
subskills.description: JavaScript libraries for blockchain interaction. ethers.js v6: Provider (read-only blockchain connection), Signer (transaction signing), Contract (typed contract interaction with ABI), Wallet, utils (parseEther, formatEther, keccak256, solidityKeccak256, hexlify). Viem as the modern TypeScript alternative (public client, wallet client, type-safe ABI). web3.js v4 (older, less favored). Moralis SDK: abstraction layer offering token balances, NFT metadata, transaction history, and real-time streams without direct RPC calls. wagmi/core for framework-agnostic wallet management.

subskills.name: Client Nodes (Geth, Besu, Nethermind, Substrate)
subskills.description: Running your own Ethereum or Substrate nodes for maximum control, privacy, and performance. Ethereum execution clients: Geth (Go — most popular, full node, light node, snap sync, archive node), Besu (Java — ConsenSys enterprise client, EEA private transactions, privacy groups, PoA networks), Nethermind (.NET — fast sync, Prometheus metrics, plugin system). Consensus layer clients: Prysm, Lighthouse, Lodestar (for post-Merge validator node operation). Substrate node for Polkadot/Kusama parachain development. Node sync modes, archive vs pruned, and JSON-RPC API.
